explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `barT φ` is the library's own definition `φ.symm (star (φ x))`, and `IsCoord` is the library's own predicate. It requires the ring equivalence φ to send `z ⊗ₜ r` to r times the coordinate-wise image of z. The theorem says that, under this predicate, `barT φ` acts on pure tensors as conjugation on the first factor. All of that content comes from these two library definitions. The proof only uses library lemmas (`φ_barT`, `hφ.tmul`, `hatQ_star`) plus routine `ext`/`simp` on quaternion components. Mathlib has no statement about `barT` or `IsCoord`. The one Mathlib-style fact it relates to, that `star` on a tensor product of quaternion algebras acts on the left factor, does not appear in Mathlib in a form that applies directly to this arbitrary ring equivalence φ. I only checked the two definitions in the library file; I did not grep Mathlib by name or content, so this is an inference from the definitions rather than the result of a search.
